issues.title: WSL 2.7.3: /mnt/shared_memory missing → WSLg windows invisible ([WARN:COPY MODE])
issues.next_action_reason: Community-confirmed 2.7.3 regression with root cause + workaround and multiple me-toos, but no team acknowledgement in ~67 days. Acknowledge, label, route to maintainer, and ask latest-build confirmation + cold-boot logs.
issues.suggested_reply:
Thanks @neumaennl for the detailed diagnosis, and thanks to everyone confirming — this is very helpful. To summarize what the thread has established:

- After updating to WSL 2.7.3+, `/mnt/shared_memory` is no longer mounted at WSLg startup, so `rdp_allocate_shared_memory` fails with `Input/output error` and Weston falls back to `[WARN:COPY MODE]`, leaving GUI windows invisible.
- Workaround: create the mount and persist it via `/etc/fstab` (`tmpfs /mnt/shared_memory tmpfs defaults 0 0`) with `mountFsTab=true` in `/etc/wsl.conf`.
- It reproduces on 2.7.3 through 2.7.11 and appears non-deterministic across `wsl --shutdown` / Windows reboot.

We're treating this as a 2.7.3 regression in the shared-memory setup path and will route it internally. Could a couple of you confirm whether it still repros on the very latest WSL pre-release, and share `/mnt/wslg/weston.log` + `dmesg` from a cold boot where it's broken (the `InitEntryUtilityVm ... Init has exited` line @neumaennl saw suggests VM-init timing may be involved)? That will help pin down whether the mount race is in WSL init or WSLg.

issues.title: [ARM64 / Qualcomm Adreno 680] GPU acceleration unavailable in WSL2 — /dev/dri/renderD128 not created by dxgkrnl, Mesa falls back to llvmpipe

issues.suggested_reply: Thanks for the detailed diagnosis, @dorepi — and @Gerdya/@baluyotraf for confirming. GPU acceleration in WSLg depends on the Windows-side GPU vendor driver exposing GPU paravirtualization (WDDM 2.9+/GPU-PV); when that's present, dxgkrnl creates /dev/dri/renderD128 and Mesa's d3d12 backend can bind. On Qualcomm Adreno the WDDM driver has historically not exposed GPU-PV, which is why you see the llvmpipe fallback despite /dev/dxg and the /usr/lib/wsl/lib bridge being in place. Could you share the exact Adreno driver version (from Windows Device Manager) and the output of wsl --version? We'll label this GPU and track it against Qualcomm driver support.
